title: A scalable suspension insect cell transfection method for production of baculoviruses with low amplification passages
author: Cabral, Garcia, et al.
materials: With the employment of the BEV system Bac-to-Bac HBM-TOPO purchased from Thermo Scientific/Invitrogen, construction of recombinant bacmids were performed for ten different protein encoding genes (Table 1). The Bac-to-Bac HBM-TOPO system is based on AcMNPV and the recombinant expression is driven by the Polyhedrin gene promoter associated to a honeybee melitin (HBM) exportation signal at the N-terminus that has the function to transport the product to the extracellular medium. The vector also presents a C-terminal tag of six histidines (his-tag) to facilitate protein purification using affinity chromatography which is preceded by the Tobacco Etch Virus (TEV) protease signal peptide. The encoding sequences described in Table 1 were amplified by PCR with the Platinum Taq High Fidelity (ThermoFisher Scientific/Invitrogen) and blunt ended fragments were obtained by treatment of the amplicons with the proofreading Pfx Taq DNA polymerase (ThermoFisher Scientific/Invitrogen) for 30 min at 74 °C to remove the adenine 3′OH overhang added by the proofreading Platinum Taq High Fidelity DNA polymerase. This procedure was necessary since not all fragments could be obtained directly by PCR with Pfx Taq DNA polymerase. steps.title: Amplify coding sequences by PCR
steps.instruction: Amplify each target gene using Platinum Taq High Fidelity polymerase (ThermoFisher Scientific/Invitrogen) according to standard PCR conditions.

steps.title: Blunt‑end PCR amplicons
steps.instruction: Treat the amplicons with Pfx Taq DNA polymerase (ThermoFisher Scientific/Invitrogen) for 30 min at 74 °C to remove the 3′‑A overhang and generate blunt‑ended fragments.

steps.title: Clone into HBM‑TOPO and generate bacmid
steps.instruction: Ligate the blunt‑ended fragments into the HBM‑TOPO donor plasmid and perform transposition into the bacmid in DH10B E. coli following the Bac‑to‑Bac HBM‑TOPO manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Prepare transfection mixtures
steps.instruction: In two separate 1.5 mL microtubes add 350 µL of ESF‑921 or SF900III medium, 8 µL Cellfectin® Reagent (Invitrogen) and 6 µg (1 µg/µL) purified recombinant baculovirus DNA; incubate 10 min at room temperature, then mix the Cellfectin® and DNA solutions together and incubate an additional 30 min at room temperature to form the transfection mixture.

steps.title: Grow Sf9 suspension cells
steps.instruction: Culture Sf9 cells in 250 mL polycarbonate Erlenmeyer flasks (Nunc) containing up to 100 mL ESF‑921 or SF900III medium, shaken at 100 rpm, 28 °C, protected from light, until the density reaches 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL with >95 % viability (assessed with 0.5 % trypan blue).

steps.title: Harvest and resuspend cells in transfection mix
steps.instruction: Collect 6 mL of the 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL culture by centrifugation at 200 × g for 10 min at room temperature; discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in the prepared transfection mixture and incubate at room temperature for 4–5 h.

steps.title: Post‑transfection incubation
steps.instruction: After the 4–5 h incubation, centrifuge the cells again at 200 × g for 15 min at room temperature, remove the supernatant, gently resuspend the pellet in 12 mL of fresh ESF‑921 or SF900III medium, transfer to a sterile 25 mL polycarbonate Erlenmeyer flask and incubate on a shaker at 100 rpm, 28 °C for 96 h.

steps.title: Monitor cytopathic effects
steps.instruction: At 24, 48, 72 and 96 h post‑transfection, withdraw aliquots, add 0.5 % trypan blue, count cells in a hemocytometer under an optical microscope and record viability and cytopathic morphology.

steps.title: Calculate transfection efficiency
steps.instruction: Determine the percentage of trypan‑blue‑positive cells that display enlarged nuclei and membranes and vacuolar structures (characteristic of baculovirus infection) at 48–72 h post‑transfection.

steps.title: Estimate recombinant baculovirus titer
steps.instruction: Estimate virus titer by counting the number of infected (blue‑stained) cells showing cytopathic effects at 48–72 h and assuming each infected cell produces 100 virus particles.

steps.title: First virus amplification (passage 1)
steps.instruction: Inoculate 240 mL of Sf9 culture (1 × 10⁶ cells/mL, >95 % viability) with the transfection supernatant at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 1; incubate 96 h at 28 °C, 100 rpm and estimate the resulting titer (~1 × 10⁸ viruses/mL).

steps.title: Second virus amplification (passage 2)
steps.instruction: Inoculate 100 mL of fresh Sf9 culture (1 × 10⁶ cells/mL, >95 % viability) with 1 mL of the passage‑1 virus stock (MOI = 1); incubate 96 h under the same conditions to obtain a virus stock >1 × 10⁸ viruses/mL.

steps.title: Scale‑up final virus stock
steps.instruction: From the two amplification passages, produce up to 24 L of virus stock at a concentration of 1 × 10⁸ viruses/mL.
